texts: good. the log entry seals cleanly as a reported (not asserted) claim, with the bright lantern, the crowd and the nightmoth kind all carried inside it. One caveat no rewrite can fix: our calendar terms offer only a day-of-month slot, so 'day 396' is stored there — the number survives but the slot does not mean day-of-year, and we have filed that as a gap on our side.

mixed: the crowd, the sky-cats and the 'from the cliff-spires' origin all come through, but the direction word 'down' is dropped with no trace — the particle is separated from its verb by the object, and we only keep a particle that sits next to the verb. Rewrite as 'Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a crowd of nightmoths brings down sky-cats from the cliff-spires.', which keeps 'brings down' as one verb and leaves everything else unchanged.

bad: 'during hunts' is only a time anchor in your sentence, but the parse turns it into a claim that each sky-cat is the hunter — content we invent that your words never state. If the sky-cats are the hunters, say so: 'Coraline Ash wrote in her log that sky-cats molt while they hunt.' If the hunts are someone else's, name whose they are instead.

good. it becomes a per-feather conditional inside the log report, with the resulting 'safe' state reified and tied to the making, and the Sunken Cove's name and kind kept outside the report where they belong. One check on your side: we read 'ground' as 'ground up' and attach it as a property of the feathers, so if you meant feathers lying on the ground, phrase it that way.

mixed: the reading, Pell as the addressee and the past tense all land, but 'at breakfast' has no licensed time slot for us — a meal name is neither a clock/calendar term nor one of the day-parts we accept (morning/afternoon/evening/night/dawn/noon/dusk) — so it currently sits in the time slot as a bare symbol. Rewrite as 'Coraline Ash read the log entry to Pell during breakfast.': 'during' routes breakfast through the event-anchor form we do license, and 'the log entry' ties what she read back to the log she wrote in, which 'the note' does not (it mints an unrelated new referent).
